messages:
sam: quick q — for infra-only changes (build flags, dockerfile, autoscale tweaks) do we always bump patch? trying to standardize tagging so downstream teams can rely on pins
anya: if it doesn't change public API or surface, patch sounds right. but call out perf-impacting infra in the notes
jess: agreed on patch for non-consumer changes. only escalate to minor if there's a behavior change consumers could observe (response schema, tokens, etc.)
liam: one wrinkle: some teams pin ~1.4.x which lets them pull minors. if we accidentally do minor for infra, they might see unexpected changes. recommend err on patch unless clearly breaking
sam: thanks. one more: metadata in the tag — do we prefer hyphen suffix (v1.4.3-infra.202603) or +buildmeta (v1.4.3+infra.202603)? or both?
jess: pref hyphen. easier to grep and sort in git tags. + is legal semver build metadata but some tooling strips it in places
liam: + can be lost in certain clients. hyphen (pre-release style) signals it's not a breaking API bump. maybe: vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH-infra.YYYYMMDD-HHMM
anya: sounds good. also propose a conv: patch-only infra -> add "infra" suffix; hotfix rollback -> "hotfix"; any security patch -> "sec" prefix in release notes even if tag is patch
sam: deploy-bot started canary now so this is timely:
```
deploy-bot: [1934567902] deploy canary -> prod-3 (image: registry/redwood/api@sha256:abc123)
Tags: v1.4.3-infra.20260321-1532
Checks: smoke ok, latency p95 baseline within 5%.
```
liam: if canary p99 >20% rollback. also if errors spike >1% of requests. keep thresholds strict for infra changes that touch runtime config
jess: +1 to thresholds. add a quick perf checklist to release notes so oncall knows what to check during rollout
anya: wording for release notes: short bullet: "infra: updated runtime flags and build config. No API changes. Monitor p95/p99 and errors." keep it explicit for downstream teams
sam: ok i'm going to document the policy: 1) default bump = patch for infra-only; 2) tag format = vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH-<kind>.<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>; 3) call out perf-impact and SLO thresholds in notes; 4) minor bump only for consumer-visible changes. i'll open a tiny RFC and add examples
deploy-bot: [1934567915] canary health: smoke ✅, p95 +3%, p99 +9%, errors stable. continuing rollout to 50%
sam: perfect. thanks all — will post RFC and a small release-note template
